ELMALILI:53:23-25#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:23-25#2/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:53:23-25#2/r1.claim: Because the surah says Muhammad does not speak from caprice, a satanic insertion cannot have entered his delivery of revelation.
ELMALILI:53:23-25#2/r1.anchor: “Ve’n-Necmi” sûresini okurken lisân-ı Muhammedîden hevâ ile bir söz sudûruna ihtimal olmadığı

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p9/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p9/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p9/r14.claim: “Your companion” is Muḥammad, addressed by Quraysh; he is guided and rightly directed, contrary to their accusation of error and misguidance.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p9/r14.anchor: صاحبكم: هو محمد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، والخطاب لقريش: أي هو مهتد راشد

STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r10.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r10.claim: The opening responds to the disbelievers’ claim in 52:33 that the Prophet invented the revelation.
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r10.anchor: the opening verses respond to the contention of the disbelievers in 52:33, He has invented it

STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r11.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r11.claim: The sūrah is famous for its rhetorical power and the dispute over the meaning of its opening section.
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r11.anchor: because of its poetic rhetorical power and the debate that arises

STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r12.speaker: many commentators
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r12.claim: Many commentators identify the passage as the Prophet’s two visions of Gabriel in his true form, unlike Gabriel’s usual human appearance.
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r12.anchor: Many commentators say the passage refers to the Prophet’s two visions of the Archangel Gabriel in his true form

STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r13.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r13.speaker: many others
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r13.claim: Many others read the passage as the Prophet seeing God, by heart alone or by both eye and heart, during the Night Journey and Ascension.
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r13.anchor: Many others interpret it as a reference to the Prophet’s vision of God

RAZI-FULL:v28p239/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p239/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p239/r1.claim: The opening matches al-Ṭūr’s close in wording through the shared star reference and in meaning: its night-and-stars conclusion leads into the staged account of the Prophet’s opponents.
RAZI-FULL:v28p239/r1.anchor: أول هذه السورة مناسب لآخر ما قبلها لفظا ومعنى

RAZI-FULL:v28p241#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p241#3/r1.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v28p241#3/r1.claim: Some exegetes distinguish ḍalāl as the opposite of guidance and ghayy as the opposite of right conduct; Rāzī says most commentators do not distinguish them.
RAZI-FULL:v28p241#3/r1.anchor: الضلال في مقابلة الهدى ، والغي في مقابلة الرشد

RAZI-FULL:v28p241#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p241#3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p241#3/r2.claim: Rāzī says ḍalāl is broader in ordinary usage: a traveler may lose every route to a destination, while ghayy describes having no straight route; hence a sinner may be foolish or unrighteous without being called astray.

RAZI-FULL:v28p241#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p241#3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p241#3/r3.claim: On this distinction, “he did not stray” denies unbelief, while “he did not go astray” denies even the lesser fault of sinful conduct; Rāzī also compares ḍalāl to nonexistence and ghayy to corrupt existence.
RAZI-FULL:v28p241#3/r3.anchor: ولا أقل من ذلك فما فسق

RAZI-FULL:v28p241#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p241#3/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p241#3/r4.claim: Alternatively, Rāzī ranks ḍalāl like nonexistence and ghayy like corrupt existence.

RAZI-FULL:v28p241#3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p241#3/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p241#3/r5.claim: “Your ṣāḥib” can mean your master or your companion.

RAZI-FULL:v28p241#3/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p241#3/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p241#3/r6.claim: Rāzī allows “did not stray” to mean “was not insane,” since a madman is described as astray; he links the denial to the assurance that the Prophet is a wise guide to God.
RAZI-FULL:v28p241#3/r6.anchor: فإن المجنون ضال ، وعلى هذا فهو كقوله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v28p241#3/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p241#3/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p241#3/r7.claim: The sequence presents him as on the right path, then on a straight path, then as swiftly following its course; alternatively, not speaking from desire proves he cannot be led astray by desire.
RAZI-FULL:v28p241#3/r7.anchor: قال أولا { ما ضل } أي هو على الطريق { وما غوى }

RAZI-FULL:v28p241#3/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p241#3/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p241#3/r8.claim: The past-tense denials can describe the Prophet’s protected earlier life, including his childhood and retreat; his present speech is now revelation that rescues and guides others.
RAZI-FULL:v28p241#3/r8.anchor: وصار الآن منقذا من الضلالة ومرشدا وهاديا

RAZI-FULL:v28p241#3/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p241#3/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p241#3/r9.claim: God preserves someone destined for prophethood from unbelief and grave vices in youth; Rāzī applies this protection to the Prophet’s earlier life.
RAZI-FULL:v28p241#3/r9.anchor: يصون من يريد إرساله في صغره

RAZI-FULL:v28p241#3/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p241#3/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p241#3/r10.claim: Rāzī treats hawā here as the soul’s base appetite: its letters suggest falling and lowliness, and Qur’anic usage sets it against praiseworthy love; he cites the soul restrained from desire.
RAZI-FULL:v28p241#3/r10.anchor: لم يستعمل الهوى إلا في المواضع الذي يخالف المحبة

STUDYQURAN:53:2/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:2/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:2/r1.claim: “Your companion” refers to the Prophet Muhammad.
STUDYQURAN:53:2/r1.anchor: Your companion refers to the Prophet Muhammad.

STUDYQURAN:53:2/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:2/r2.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:53:2/r2.claim: Some take ḍalla, being astray, as the opposite of guidance (hudā).
STUDYQURAN:53:2/r2.anchor: Some maintain that“to be astray” or “to stray” (ḍalla

STUDYQURAN:53:2/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:2/r3.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:53:2/r3.claim: R identifies ghawā, to err, as the opposite of sound judgment (rushd); R is also cited among those explaining erring as ignorance from adherence to corrupt creed.
STUDYQURAN:53:2/r3.anchor: err” is also understood to indicate ignorance that results from adhering to a corrupt creed (Iṣ, R, Ṭb).

STUDYQURAN:53:2/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:2/r4.speaker: Iṣ, R, Ṭb
STUDYQURAN:53:2/r4.claim: Other commentators understand erring as ignorance caused by adherence to a corrupt creed.
STUDYQURAN:53:2/r4.anchor: “To err” is also understood to indicate ignorance that results from adhering to a corrupt creed (Iṣ, R, Ṭb).

STUDYQURAN:53:2/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:2/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:2/r5.claim: On this distinction, straying is lack of guidance, while erring is following religion incorrectly.
STUDYQURAN:53:2/r5.anchor: In this sense, “to be astray” indicates the absence of guidance, while “to err” indicates that one is mistaken in how one follows religion.

STUDYQURAN:53:2/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:2/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:2/r7.claim: The Prophet's lack of caprice means he did not author revelation and his own speech is guided; together, the claims affirm true religion, correct practice, and freedom from whim.
STUDYQURAN:53:2/r7.anchor: That the Prophet does not speak out of caprice indicates both that he did not author the revelation himself and that his own speech is guided.

TAB-FULL:v22p7/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p7/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v22p7/r3.claim: Muhammad has not departed from the truth or gone astray from it; he is instead on a straight and sound course.
TAB-FULL:v22p7/r3.anchor: ما حاد صاحبكم أيها الناس عن الحق ولا زال عنه، ولكنه على استقامة وسداد

BURSEVI:v9p172#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p172#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p172#3/r4.claim: The oath's answer is that Muhammad never left the path of truth, the road of the afterlife.
BURSEVI:v9p172#3/r4.anchor: هو جواب القسم أي ما عدل عن طريق الحق الذي هو مسلك الآخرة

BURSEVI:v9p172#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p172#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p172#3/r5.claim: This denies the kind of error alleged by the phrase 'He found you astray' in 93:7: before and after revelation the Prophet worshipped God, affirmed unity, and avoided reprehensible conduct.
BURSEVI:v9p172#3/r5.anchor: وهذا دليل على أن قوله ووجدك ضالا ليس من ضلال الغي فإنه عليه السلام قبل الوحي وبعده لم يزل يعبد ربه ويوحده

BURSEVI:v9p172#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p172#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p172#3/r6.claim: The contrast with Adam, of whom scripture says he disobeyed and went astray, highlights the Prophet's virtue: God says Muhammad did not stray or err.
BURSEVI:v9p172#3/r6.anchor: وفيه بيان فضل النبي عليه السلام حيث أن الله تعالى قال في حق آدم

BURSEVI:v9p172#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p172#3/r7.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v9p172#3/r7.claim: Al-Raghib defines ghayy as ignorance grounded in a false belief, unlike a complete absence of belief; it is narrower than ḍalāl, which includes errors of speech, action, character, and belief.
BURSEVI:v9p172#3/r7.anchor: قال الراغب الغي جهل من اعتقاد فاسد وذلك أن الجهل قد يكون من كون الإنسان غير معتقد أصلا

BURSEVI:v9p172#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p172#3/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p172#3/r8.claim: Ghayy is specified after the broader term ḍalāl to emphasize sound belief; the Prophet never held a false belief and possessed complete guidance.
BURSEVI:v9p172#3/r8.anchor: فعطفه على ما ضل من عطف الخاص على العام للاهتمام بشأن الاعتقاد بمعنى أنه فرق بين الغي والضلال

BURSEVI:v9p172#3/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p172#3/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p172#3/r9.claim: Quraysh accused Muhammad of leaving his ancestors' religion and speaking on his own; this sūra answers them, and 'your companion' reminds them they knew his blameless life and excellent guidance.
BURSEVI:v9p172#3/r9.anchor: وكانوا يقولون ضل محمد عن دين آبائه وخرج عن الطريق وتقول شيئا من تلقاء نفسه فرد الله عليهم بنفسه

TABATABAI:53:1-2/r14.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:1-2/r14.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:1-2/r14.claim: Deviation is departure from the straight path; ghayy contrasts with right guidance and attaining what is true.
TABATABAI:53:1-2/r14.anchor: الضلال الخروج والانحراف عن الصراط المستقيم

TABATABAI:53:1-2/r15.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:1-2/r15.speaker: الراغب
TABATABAI:53:1-2/r15.claim: Al-Raghib defines ghayy as ignorance based on a false belief, unlike ignorance where a person holds neither a sound nor false belief.
TABATABAI:53:1-2/r15.anchor: قال الراغب الغي جهل من اعتقاد فاسد

TABATABAI:53:1-2/r16.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:1-2/r16.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:1-2/r16.anchor: والمراد بالصاحب هو النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

TABATABAI:53:1-2/r17.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:1-2/r17.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:1-2/r17.claim: The Prophet neither missed the human destination of happiness—servitude to God—nor the path leading to it, in belief or judgment.
TABATABAI:53:1-2/r17.anchor: أنه لم يخطئ لا في الغاية المطلوبة

TABRISI:53:1-10/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:1-10/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:53:1-10/r7.claim: Ghayy means failure, as in ghawāya and ghawā.

TABRISI:53:2-5/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:2-5/r1.speaker: حسان
TABRISI:53:2-5/r1.claim: Hassan's poem recounts an attacker who threw at the Messenger, was struck by a dog, and whose fate is called a lesson for leader and follower.
TABRISI:53:2-5/r1.anchor: يقول حسان: سائل بني الأصفر إن جئته ما كان أنباء بني واسع

TABRISI:53:2-5/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:2-5/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:53:2-5/r2.claim: The Prophet did not leave truth or guidance, nor err in what he conveyed; the second phrase reinforces the first because ghawā also means straying.
TABRISI:53:2-5/r2.anchor: أي ما عدل عن الحق وما فارق الهدى إلى الضلال وما غوى فيما يؤديه إليكم

TABRISI:53:2-5/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:2-5/r3.speaker: غير مسمى
TABRISI:53:2-5/r3.claim: One alternative says the Prophet did not fail to attain right guidance.

TABRISI:53:2-5/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:2-5/r4.speaker: غير مسمى
TABRISI:53:2-5/r4.claim: Another says his effort did not fail, since he receives God's reward and honor.
TABRISI:53:2-5/r4.anchor: ما خاب سعيه بل ينال ثواب الله وكرامته

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p11#4/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p11#4/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p11#4/r1.claim: The companion is Muhammad, who did not stray from the path of guidance or go astray.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p11#4/r1.anchor: يعني النبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم- يقول: ما ضل عن طريق الهدى وما غوى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p11#4/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p11#4/r2.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p11#4/r2.claim: Muqatil says the verse means that Muhammad did not speak falsehood.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p11#4/r2.anchor: قال مقاتل: يعني ما تكلم بالباطل

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:1-8/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:1-8/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:1-8/r3.claim: The Prophet who did not stray is Muhammad.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:1-8/r3.anchor: ما ضل صاحبكم } محمد عليه السلام { وما غوى

QASHANI:53:1-6/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:53:1-6/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:53:1-6/r2.claim: The Prophet did not go astray by stopping at the self or inclining toward it instead of the ultimate aim.
QASHANI:53:1-6/r2.anchor: بالوقوف مع النفس والانحراف عن المقصد الأقصى بالميل لها

QASHANI:53:1-6/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:53:1-6/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:53:1-6/r3.claim: He did not stray through being veiled by attributes or stopping with them at the station of the heart.
QASHANI:53:1-6/r3.anchor: بالاحتجاب بالصفات والوقوف معها في مقام القلب

ELMALILI:53:1-7/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:1-7/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:53:1-7/r19.claim: If najm is the Quran, its descent is the moment of each revelation; the oath by the moment of revelation confirms the following assertion with emphasis.
ELMALILI:53:1-7/r19.anchor: Kur’ân’ın necmi olduğuna göre ise “hüviy” onun nüzûlü demektir

ELMALILI:53:1-7/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:1-7/r20.speaker: author
ELMALILI:53:1-7/r20.claim: Dalal is the opposite of guidance: losing one's way or being unable to find a way; ghayy is the opposite of right-mindedness, losing sound judgment or the straight road.

ELMALILI:53:1-7/r21.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:1-7/r21.speaker: author
ELMALILI:53:1-7/r21.claim: The companion is Muhammad, and the address is directed to Quraysh and their like, who accused him of inventing the Quran.
ELMALILI:53:1-7/r21.anchor: “Sâhib”den murad, Muhammed Mustafa sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem’dir. Hitab da ona “Kur’ân’ı kendi uyduruyor” diyen Kureyş ve eşbâhınadır

ELMALILI:53:1-7/r22.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:1-7/r22.speaker: author
ELMALILI:53:1-7/r22.claim: Calling him their companion stresses that they know him from close association as sound-minded, and that he is their friend and protector seeking to guide them; he neither goes astray nor loses his mind, deceives, nor is deceived.
ELMALILI:53:1-7/r22.anchor: sâhib dâima sohbette bulunan arkadaş ve sahâbet edip koruyan hâmî mânalarını ifade ettiği için şu meâli ifade eder

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:1/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:1/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:1/r2.claim: The Prophet was neither astray nor acting from personal ambition; he did not depart from what revelation and reason require, affirming divine protection from harmful influences.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:1/r2.anchor: onun yolunu şaşırmış bir insan olmadığı gibi kişisel ihtiraslarıyla da hareket etmediği, vahyin ve aklın icaplarından sapmadığı belirtilmektedir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:1/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:1/r3.speaker: Şevkânî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:1/r3.claim: Shawkānī says “your companion” recalls that the audience knew the Prophet closely.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:1/r3.anchor: sâhibüküm tamlamasının kullanılmış olması, muhatapların Hz. Peygamber’i yakından tanıdıklarını (Şevkânî, V, 122)

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:1/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:1/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:1/r4.claim: The word sahib is apt because it is used especially for people who have spent a long time together; sohbet shares the same root.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:1/r4.anchor: sâhib kelimesi daha çok, uzun süre birlikte olmuş kişiler hakkında kullanılır; dilimizdeki “sohbet” kelimesi de aynı kökten türetilmiştir

QUSHAYRI:v3p247/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p247/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p247/r9.claim: The Prophet never strayed from monotheism, and ghayy is the opposite of right guidance.
QUSHAYRI:v3p247/r9.anchor: الغي : نقيض الرشد . . وفي هذا تخصيص للنبي

QUSHAYRI:v3p247/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p247/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p247/r10.claim: God directly defends the Prophet here, unlike Noah and Hud who answered their accusers themselves, or Moses who rebuked Pharaoh.
QUSHAYRI:v3p247/r10.anchor: وفي هذا تخصيص للنبي حيث تولى - سبحانه - الذب عنه فيما رمي به

QUSHAYRI:v3p247/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p247/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p247/r11.claim: The Prophet never lost awareness of witnessing, even for an instant.
QUSHAYRI:v3p247/r11.anchor: ما ضل صاحبكم ، ولا غفل عن الشهود طرفة عين

BURHAN:v1p77/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p77/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p77/r2.claim: The finest sajʿ has equal clauses, resembling poetry's equal-length lines; extending a cadence after the ear expects its endpoint makes the excess feel heavy.
BURHAN:v1p77/r2.anchor: وأحسن السجع ما تساوت قرائنه ليكون شبيها بالشعر فإن أبياته متساوية

BURHAN:v1p77/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p77/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p77/r3.claim: A balanced cadence can be followed by a longer second clause, as in ما ضل صاحبكم وما غوى, or by a longer third clause, as in the command to take and bind the condemned man.

SULAMI:v2p283#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p283#2/r1.speaker: جعفر
SULAMI:v2p283#2/r1.claim: The Prophet never strayed from nearness to God, even for an instant.
SULAMI:v2p283#2/r1.anchor: قال جعفر : ما ضل عن قربه طرفة عين

SULAMI:v2p283#2/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p283#2/r2.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p283#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAtaʾ interprets the verse as saying the Prophet never strayed from witnessing God, even for an instant.
SULAMI:v2p283#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن عطاء رحمة الله عليه يقول : ﴿ ما ضل ﴾ عن الرؤية طرفة عين

SULAMI:v2p283#2/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p283#2/r3.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v2p283#2/r3.claim: The Prophet never departed from the reality of divine oneness or followed Satan.
SULAMI:v2p283#2/r3.anchor: قال سهل : ﴿ ما ضل ﴾ عن حقيقة التوحيد قط ولا اتبع الشيطان بحال

ITQAN:v3p280/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p280/r1.speaker: أهل البديع
ITQAN:v3p280/r1.claim: Rhetoricians say the best rhymed cadence has equal endings, with the second clause longer as a next-best pattern and the third clause longer in a three-part series.
ITQAN:v3p280/r1.anchor: قال أهل البديع أحسن السجع ونحوه ما تساوت قرائنه نحو

ITQAN:v3p280/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p280/r2.speaker: ابن الأثير
ITQAN:v3p280/r2.claim: Ibn al-Athir says the second ending should match the first or be slightly longer, and the third should be longer.
ITQAN:v3p280/r2.anchor: وقال ابن الأثير الأحسن في الثانية المساواة

ITQAN:v3p280/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p280/r3.speaker: الخفاجي
ITQAN:v3p280/r3.claim: Al-Khafaji says the second ending must never be shorter than the first.
ITQAN:v3p280/r3.anchor: وقال الخفاجي لا يجوز أن تكون الثانية أقصر من الأولى

ITQAN:v3p280/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p280/r4.speaker: قائلون
ITQAN:v3p280/r4.claim: Another rule favors short cadence units because they display the speaker's strength; the minimum is two words, long units exceed ten, and those between are medium, as in Surat al-Qamar.
ITQAN:v3p280/r4.anchor: الثاني قالوا أحسن السجع ما كان قصيرا لدلالته على قوة المنشئ

ITQAN:v3p280/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p280/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
ITQAN:v3p280/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says preserving verse endings is good only when meaning and sound remain coherent; polishing sound while neglecting meaning is not eloquence.
ITQAN:v3p280/r5.anchor: قال الزمخشري في كشافه القديم لا تحسن المحافظ على الفواصل لمجردها

ITQAN:v3p280/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p280/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
ITQAN:v3p280/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the fronting in 2:4 is for exclusivity, not merely to fit the verse ending.
ITQAN:v3p280/r6.anchor: وبني على ذلك أن التقديم في ﴿ وبالآخرة هم يوقنون ﴾ ليس لمجرد الفاصلة بل لرعاية الاختصاص

ITQAN:v3p280/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p280/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p280/r7.claim: Verse endings are based on pausal forms, allowing a nominative ending to match a genitive one and vice versa; the source illustrates this with several paired passages.
ITQAN:v3p280/r7.anchor: مبنى الفواصل على الوقف ولهذا ساغ مقابلة المرفوع بالمجرور وبالعكس كقوله

ITQAN:v3p280/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p280/r8.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p280/r8.claim: Qur'anic endings often use long vowels and an appended nūn to sustain melodic extension; Sībawayh notes that Arabic singers append these sounds to lengthen the voice, and the Qur'an uses easy pauses and sweet endings.
ITQAN:v3p280/r8.anchor: كثر في القرآن ختم الفواصل بحروف المد واللين وإلحاق النون وحكمته وجود التمكن من التطريب بذلك

TUSTARI:53:2/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:53:2/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:53:2/r1.claim: The Prophet never strayed from the reality of divine oneness and never followed Satan.
TUSTARI:53:2/r1.anchor: أي ما ضل عن حقيقة التوحيد قط، ولا اتبع الشيطان بحال

DAMGHANI:v1p274/r3.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p274/r3.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p274/r3.claim: Al-ṣāḥib can refer to the Prophet: the verse denies that your prophet is mad.
DAMGHANI:v1p274/r3.anchor: وما صاحبكم بمجنون يعني وما نبيكم بمجنون

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p392/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p392/r2.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p392/r2.claim: Sahib refers to the Prophet in 53:2 and 81:22.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p392/r2.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن الصاحب في القرآن على تسعة أوجه : - أحدها : النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

FARRA:v3p94/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p94/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p94/r4.claim: The statement that the Prophet did not stray is the answer to the oath.

MAJAZ:v2p235/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p235/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p235/r2.claim: Ghawā is from al-ghayy, and al-ghāwī is the person who strays.

MAJAZ:v2p235/r3.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p235/r3.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p235/r3.claim: He reports an alternative dialectal analysis, غوى يغوي like shaqiya yashqā; this usage is also said of a calf that becomes overfull or sick from milk.

NAHHAS:v4p265/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p265/r2.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p265/r2.claim: The Prophet did not depart from the right course.
NAHHAS:v4p265/r2.anchor: أي ما زال عن القصد ( وما غوى )

NAHHAS:v4p265/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p265/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p265/r3.claim: One explanation says he did not fail to attain the mercy he sought.
NAHHAS:v4p265/r3.anchor: قيل أي وما خاب فيما طلبه من الرحمة

SAMIN-DURR:53:2-3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:53:2-3/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:53:2-3/r1.claim: ما ضل صاحبكم is the answer to the oath.
SAMIN-DURR:53:2-3/r1.anchor: وقوله: { ما ضل صاحبكم }: هذا جواب القسم.

ZAJJAJ:v5p69/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p69/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p69/r7.claim: The verse is the answer to the oath by the star.
ZAJJAJ:v5p69/r7.anchor: ما ضل صاحبكم وما غوى (2) جواب القسم

ZAJJAJ:v5p69/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p69/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p69/r8.claim: The companion addressed is the Prophet.
ZAJJAJ:v5p69/r8.anchor: يعني النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

ASAD-NOTES:53:1#n2/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:53:1#n2/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:53:1#n2/r1.claim: Asad directs readers to note 150 on 7:184 for this description of Muhammad.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p109/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p109/r1.speaker: القاضي عبد الجبار
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p109/r1.claim: Al-Qadi argues that Arab experience let eloquent listeners recognize the Qur'an's extraordinary eloquence without a fresh trial; those less eloquent would see its inimitability even more readily.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p109/r1.anchor: وعقد القاضي فصلاً (في اختصاص القرآن بمزية في رتبة الفصاحة خارجة عن العادة)

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p109/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p109/r2.speaker: بعض شيوخنا
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p109/r2.claim: Some of the author's teachers answered a Jewish denial of the Qur'an's distinctive merit by reciting Qur'anic passages whose eloquence is self-evident.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p109/r2.anchor: وقد أورد بعض شيوخنا عند جحد بعض اليهود أن للقرآن مزية

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p109/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p109/r3.speaker: القاضي عبد الجبار
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p109/r3.claim: Al-Qadi chiefly refuted opponents' attacks on the Qur'an, esoteric readings that displaced its apparent meaning, alleged contradictions, and objections to repetition or prolixity.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p109/r3.anchor: ثم كان أكثر ما تجرد له القاضي عبد الجبار: الرد على مطاعن المخالفين في القرآن

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p250/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p250/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p250/r2.claim: The oath's waaw points to the witnessed setting star and its apparent luminous link between sky and earth; this makes the descent of revelation to Muhammad less strange or disputable.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p250/r2.anchor: اللفت بالواو إلى ظاهرة كونية مشهودة، يراها الناس في النجم إذا هوى

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p49/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p49/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p49/r1.claim: Ḍalāl is broad and may be intentional or accidental; it can describe an animal losing its way, unlike ghawāya.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p49/r1.anchor: الضلالة قد تكون عن قصد أو عن غير قصد

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p49/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p49/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p49/r2.claim: Ghawāya is deliberate persistence in error, applies to morally responsible people, and contrasts with sound judgment, while ḍalāl contrasts with guidance.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p49/r2.anchor: أما الغواية فهي عن قصد وهو الإمعان في الضلال

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p49/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p49/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p49/r3.claim: Calling Muhammad “your companion” recalls his long life among them and their knowledge of his honesty, undermining accusations of deviation or madness.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p49/r3.anchor: فيهم عمراً طويلاً وخالطهم وعاشرهم وعرفوا صدقه وأمانته

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p49/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p49/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p49/r4.claim: The expression “your companion” occurs in three Quranic passages, each denying madness or deviation of the Prophet.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p49/r4.anchor: وردت صاحبكم في ثلاث مواضع في القرآن الكريم

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p49/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p49/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p49/r5.claim: The opening oath evokes falling; deviation is a moral fall, “in” misguidance suggests falling, and guidance “upon” suggests elevation and firm footing.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p49/r5.anchor: ولو لاحظنا القسم في بداية السورة هو دلالة على الهوي والسقوط

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p50/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p50/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p50/r1.claim: Repeating the negative particle before both verbs excludes both joint and separate instances of error and delusion; the Prophet is guided and rightly directed.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p50/r1.anchor: وهذا حتى لا يتصور أنه نفى الجمع بينهما فقط وإنما نفى الجمع بينهما والإفراد

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p50/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p50/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p50/r2.claim: Negating past error means he was never astray; affirmative “he was guided” might suggest a limited period or that he had been astray before guidance.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p50/r2.anchor: مهتد رشيد لم يسبق له ضلالة في أي وقت وزمن كان

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p39/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p39/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p39/r1.claim: Sūrah al-Najm is the counterpart of al-Ṭūr: both substantiate reward and punishment, though al-Ṭūr highlights torment and al-Najm refutes false intercession.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p39/r1.anchor: The central theme of both sūrahs is the same: substantiation of reward and punishment.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p39/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p39/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p39/r2.claim: False belief in intercession makes threats ineffective, so the Qur'an repeatedly joins monotheism and the Hereafter to close this escape route.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p39/r2.anchor: For this very reason, the Qur’ ān has always mentioned tawḥīd and the Hereafter side by side

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p39/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p39/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p39/r3.claim: The idolaters rely on deities that are merely invented names, not real intercessors.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p39/r3.anchor: they are mere names which they have invented

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p39/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p39/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p39/r4.claim: Even if intercessors existed, they could not add to God's knowledge, change His judgment, or turn falsehood into truth; He judges with perfect justice.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p39/r4.anchor: there is no possibility that on that day the intercession of someone may add to His information or change His decision or turn falsehood into truth.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p39/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p39/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p39/r7.claim: Verses 1–18 establish that the recited Qur'an is not soothsaying or fortune-telling but was revealed to the Prophet by God's trusted, dependable angel.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p39/r7.anchor: not the work of a soothsayer or a fortune-teller

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p39/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p39/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p39/r8.claim: The discourse presents every verse as true and inevitable, and rejects the idea that the Prophet's experiences of revelation and Gabriel are illusions.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p39/r8.anchor: All its verses are based on the truth and what is stated in them is inevitable

ALUSI-FULL:v27p45/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p45/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p45/r1.anchor: صاحبكم ( أي ما عدل عن طريق الحق

ALUSI-FULL:v27p45/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p45/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p45/r2.claim: He did not leave the true path of the Hereafter; the metaphor affirms the Prophet's words and deeds are correct.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p45/r2.anchor: أي ما عدل عن طريق الحق الذي هو مسلك الآخرة فهو استعار وتمثيل

ALUSI-FULL:v27p45/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p45/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p45/r3.claim: Ghayy means ignorance with false belief, opposite of right guidance; its coordination singles out belief as the basis of action.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p45/r3.anchor: الغي الجهل مع اعتقاد فاسد وهو خلاف الرشد

ALUSI-FULL:v27p45/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p45/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p45/r4.claim: An alternate reading praises the Qur'an as knowledge guiding to religion and truth, from which Muhammad did not stray.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p45/r4.anchor: وأما على الثالث فلأنه تنويه بشأن القرآن وتنبيه على مناط اهتدائه عليه الصلاة والسلام ومدار رشاده

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p400/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p400/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p400/r1.claim: The oath's answer says Muhammad has not strayed from guidance or gone astray.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p400/r1.anchor: يعني: محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم ما ضل عن طريق الهدى

BAYDAWI-FULL:53:1-4/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:1-4/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:1-4/r5.claim: Addressing Quraysh, the verse denies that Muḥammad departed from the straight path and rejects what they allege about him.
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:1-4/r5.anchor: ما عدل محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الطريق المستقيم

BAYDAWI-FULL:53:1-4/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:1-4/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:1-4/r6.claim: The verse also denies that Muḥammad holds a false belief, countering the accusation directed at him.

BIQAI-FULL:v7p312#2/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p312#2/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p312#2/r6.claim: The oath’s past-tense answer denies the accusations made against the Prophet even before his mission, making the inference from his earlier life especially clear.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p312#2/r6.anchor: أجابه بقوله معبرا بالماضي نفيا لما كانوا رموه به وليسهل ما قبل النبوة فيكون ما بعدها بطريقة الأولى

BIQAI-FULL:v7p313/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p313/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p313/r1.claim: The author explains the separate verse وجدك ضالا as not knowing, rather than moral misguidance.

BIQAI-FULL:v7p313/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p313/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p313/r2.claim: Calling Muhammad “your companion” invites his audience to recall their familiarity with him and makes their accusation implausible given his character and purity.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p313/r2.anchor: وعبر بالصحبة مع كونها أدل على القصد مرغبة لهم فيها ومقبلة بهم إليه ومقبحة عليهم اتهامه

BIQAI-FULL:v7p313/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p313/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p313/r3.claim: He did not deviate even slightly or intend harm; he is guarded from causes of misguidance, including devils.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p313/r3.anchor: وما مال أدنى ميل ولا كان مقصوده مما يسوء فإنه محروس من أسبابه التي هي غواية الشياطين وغيرها

BIQAI-FULL:v7p313/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p313/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p313/r4.claim: The author says God defended Muhammad, while other prophets had to deny accusations that they were misguided or foolish.

BIQAI-FULL:v7p313#2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p313#2/r4.speaker: أبو جعفر ابن الزبير
BIQAI-FULL:v7p313#2/r4.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr says the oath answers exhausted accusations, then the sura unfolds the Prophet’s closeness to God and rebukes deniers through its later signs and questions.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p313#2/r4.anchor: وقال أبو جعفر ابن الزبير في برهانه : لما قطع سبحانه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p92/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p92/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p92/r1.claim: Ḍalāl is failing to find the path to one's goal, metaphorically following a course contrary to truth.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p92/r1.anchor: والضلال : عدم الاهتداء إلى الطريق الموصل إلى المقصود ، وهو مجاز في سلوك ما ينافي الحق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p92/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p92/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p92/r2.claim: Ghawāya is corrupt judgment attached to falsehood.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p92/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p92/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p92/r3.claim: Ṣāḥib is a close associate; here it means Muhammad, who shared circumstances and events with his audience.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p92/r3.anchor: والصاحب : الملازم للذي يضاف إليه وصف صاحب ، والمراد بالصاحب هنا : الذي له ملابسات وأحوال مع المضاف إليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p92/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p92/r4.speaker: أبو معبد الخزاعي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p92/r4.claim: During the Hijra story, after the Prophet's miracle with Umm Maʿbad's ewe, Abū Maʿbad called him 'Quraysh's companion,' meaning the man involved in events between him and Quraysh.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p92/r4.anchor: وهذا كقول أبي معبد الخزاعي الوارد في أثناء قصة الهجرة لما دخل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بيته وفيها أم معبد وذكرت له معجزة مسحه على ضرع شاتها : ( هذا صاحب قريش )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p92/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p92/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p92/r5.claim: Calling him 'your companion' insinuates that his accusers are slanderers: they know his life closely because he lives among them in the same town.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p92/r5.anchor: وإيثار التعبير عنه بوصف { صاحبكم } تعريض بأنهم أهل بهتان إذ نسبوا إليه ما ليس منه في شيء مع شدة إطلاعهم على أحواله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p92/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p92/r6.speaker: الحجاج
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p92/r6.claim: Al-Ḥajjāj told the Khārijites after Dayr al-Jamājim that he knew their past betrayal and concealed unbelief, so they could not evade responsibility by equivocation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p92/r6.anchor: ووقع في خطبة الحجاج بعد دير الجماجم قوله للخوارج ( ألستم أصحابي بالأهواز حين رمتم الغدر واستبطنتم الكفر )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p92/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p92/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p92/r7.claim: The verse refutes accusations that the Prophet was insane, a magician, a poet, or that the Qur'an was fabricated: madness is misguidance, while lying and magic are misguidance and error.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p92/r7.anchor: وهذا رد من الله على المشركين وإبطال لقولهم في النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لأنهم قالوا : مجنون ، وقالوا : ساحر ، وقالوا : شاعر ، وقالوا في القرآن : إن هذا إلا اختلاق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p92/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p92/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p92/r8.claim: The familiar kind of poetry is error because its followers delight in the poets' misleading speech, as 26:224 says.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p92/r8.anchor: والشعر المتعارف بينهم غواية كما قال تعالى : { والشعراء يتبعهم الغاوون } ( الشعراء : 224 ) أي يحبذون أقوالهم لأنها غواية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p196/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p196/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p196/r3.claim: The oath answers that Muhammad neither strayed unintentionally nor chose corruption; dalāl is unintentional, while ghayy is acquired and intended. God denies both states of His Prophet.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p196/r3.anchor: والضلال أبدا يكون من غير قصد من الإنسان إليه. والغي كأنه شيء يكتسبه الإنسان ويريده

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p196/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p196/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p196/r4.claim: Ghawa means taking the path of corruption and crookedness; Muhammad was not astray on the path God set him upon, though 93:7 calls him astray before prophethood relative to his later guidance.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p196/r4.anchor: وغوى: الرجل يغوي إذا سلك سبيل الفساد والعوج، ونفى الله تعالى عن نبيه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p198#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p198#2/r2.speaker: ابن كثير وعاصم وابن عامر ونافع وأبو عمرو وحمزة والكسائي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p198#2/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir, Asim, and Ibn Amir use fatha at all verse endings; Asim in Abu Bakr's transmission uses imāla on raʾā. Nafi and Abu Amr use an intermediate form; Hamza and al-Kisai use imāla throughout, while Abu Amr in Ubayd's transmission uses it for al-aʿlā and tadallā.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p198#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وعاصم وابن عامر هذه السورة كلها بفتح أواخر آيها وأمال عاصم في رواية أبي بكر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p63/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p63/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p63/r1.claim: This is the answer to the oath: the Prophet, their companion, has not strayed from the path of guidance.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p63/r1.anchor: هذا جواب القسم والمعنى ما ضل عن طريق الهدى والمراد به رسول الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p442#3/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p442#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p442#3/r1.claim: This is the answer to the oath: it testifies that the Messenger is righteous, guided, and follows the truth, rather than being astray.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p442#3/r1.anchor: هذا هو المقسم عليه، وهو الشهادة للرسول، صلوات الله وسلامه عليه، بأنه بار راشد تابع للحق

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p442#3/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p442#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p442#3/r2.claim: A stray person is ignorant and travels without knowledge; a deviant knows the truth but deliberately turns away from it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p442#3/r2.anchor: الجاهل الذي يسلك على غير طريق بغير علم، والغاوي: هو العالم بالحق العادل عنه قصدا إلى غيره

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p442#3/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p442#3/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p442#3/r3.claim: God exonerates His Messenger and law from resemblance to Christian deviation and Jewish ways of knowing truth, concealing it, and acting against it.

JISHUMI:v9p6633/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6633/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6633/r3.claim: Al-Najm continues al-Ṭūr's close about the Prophet, his deniers, and patience by opening with the Prophet's truth and the revelation he brought.
JISHUMI:v9p6633/r3.anchor: ولما ختم سورة (الطور) بحديث النبي - صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم -، ووعيد من كذبه، وأمره بأن يصبر

JISHUMI:v9p6633/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6633/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6633/r9.claim: Ghayy means failure or loss, and ghawāya derives from it.
JISHUMI:v9p6633/r9.anchor: والغي: الخيبة، غوى يغوي، ومنه الغواية

JISHUMI:v9p6635/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6635/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6635/r2.claim: Al-najm is genitive as the object of an oath; alternatively an omitted rabb is understood. The oath's answer is that the Prophet did not stray.
JISHUMI:v9p6635/r2.anchor: والنجم كسر؛ لأنه أقسم به، وقيل: فيه إضمار، أي: ورب النجم، فيكون جر بالإضافة إليه، وجواب القسم: (ما ضل صاحبكم)

JISHUMI:v9p6635/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6635/r5.speaker: المشركون
JISHUMI:v9p6635/r5.claim: The occasion is said to be that polytheists accused Muhammad of straying from religion, so God swore that he had neither strayed nor gone astray.
JISHUMI:v9p6635/r5.anchor: قيل: إن المشركين قالوا: ضل محمد عن الدين وغوي، فأنزل الله تعالى هذه الآية، وأقسم بأنه ما ضل وما غوى

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p389#2/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p389#2/r14.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p389#2/r14.anchor: يعني : محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم , وفيه وجهان

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p389#2/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p389#2/r15.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p389#2/r15.claim: One explanation is that Muhammad did not miss the way of truth or follow falsehood.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p389#2/r15.anchor: ما ضل عن قصد الحق ولا غوى في اتباع الباطل

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p389#2/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p389#2/r16.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p389#2/r16.claim: A second explanation is that he committed no error and did not end in failure or disappointment.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p389#2/r16.anchor: ما ضل بارتكاب الضلال , وما غوى بأن خاب سعيه

MUQATIL:53:1-2/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:53:1-2/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:53:1-2/r3.claim: After Meccan unbelievers alleged Muhammad composed the Quran himself, God swears by it and says Muhammad neither strayed nor spoke falsely.
MUQATIL:53:1-2/r3.anchor: وذلك أن كفار مكة قالوا: إن محمدا يقول هذا القرآن من تلقاء نفسه

MUQATIL:53:1-2/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:53:1-2/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:53:1-2/r4.claim: The companion is Muhammad; he did not speak falsehood.
MUQATIL:53:1-2/r4.anchor: { ما ضل صاحبكم } محمد { وما غوى } [آية: 2] وما تكلم بالباطل.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p187#7/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p187#7/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p187#7/r1.claim: Muhammad, addressed here by Quraysh, did not stray from the pursuit of truth or follow falsehood.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p187#7/r1.anchor: ﴿ صاحبكم ﴾ اى محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم والخطاب لقريش

NASAFI-FULL:v4p187#7/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p187#7/r2.speaker: قيل
NASAFI-FULL:v4p187#7/r2.claim: An alternative defines ḍalāl as the opposite of guidance and ghayy as the opposite of right direction; Muhammad is guided and rightly directed, contrary to their accusation.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p187#7/r2.anchor: وقيل لاضلال نقيض الهدى والغى نقيض الرشد اى هو مهتد راشد وليس كما تزعمون من نسبتكم اياه إلى الضلال والغى

QURTUBI-FULL:53:2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:2/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:53:2/r8.claim: This is the answer to the oath: Muḥammad has not strayed from the truth or deviated from it.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:2/r8.anchor: هذا جواب القسم أي ما ضل محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الحق وما حاد عنه

QURTUBI-FULL:53:2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:2/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:53:2/r9.claim: Ghayy is the opposite of right guidance; the verse says Muḥammad did not become astray.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:2/r9.anchor: { وما غوى } الغي ضد الرشد أي ما صار غاويا

QURTUBI-FULL:53:2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:2/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:53:2/r10.claim: Other explanations are that he did not speak falsely or did not fail in what he sought, since ghayy can mean failure.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:2/r10.anchor: وقيل: أي ما تكلم بالباطل. وقيل: أي ما خاب مما طلب والغي الخيبة قال الشاعر: فمن يلق خيرا يحمد الناس أمره
